title: SLO tiering and soft-quota handoff architectural scrub
content:
Meeting objective: validate options for SLO tiering, soft-quota handoff semantics, and tenant fairness rules before writing the RFC. Attendees: Priya (chair), Marco, Evelyn, Zach, Amina. Quick context: growing Dedicated customer base requires clearer SLO tiers (bronze/silver/gold) across latency and availability. We also need a predictable soft-quota handoff to keep best-effort traffic alive without violating higher-tier guarantees. Goals: settle on policy primitives, failure semantics, metrics to expose in Console, and a migration path for existing tenants.

Summary of proposals discussed:
1) Policy primitives (Marco presented three variants):
   - Strict isolation: hard capacity partitions per tier. Simpler accounting, strong guarantees, wastes capacity under low load.
   - Soft-share with precedence: shared pool but requests carry tier precedence metadata; scheduler applies per-request priority and preemptible credits. More utilization but complex eviction semantics.
   - Hybrid windows: soft-share during normal operation, periodic balancing windows to enforce floor reserves for higher tiers. Tries to blend utilization+isolation.

2) Soft-quota handoff behaviours (Evelyn proposed state machine):
   - Grace window (configurable N seconds / tokens): when a tenant exceeds soft quota, mark requests as "best-effort" but continue serving for grace window.
   - Degradation ladder: progressively reduce batch size, switch to quantized variant, then fall back to a lower-cost model variant.
   - Handoff marker headers: responses include X-Redwood-Handoff:reason=soft_quota to surface in observability and enable automated customer notifications.

3) Tenant fairness and priority inversion mitigation (Zach):
   - Credit buckets per tenant with replenishment tied to committed capacity and recent usage.
   - Anti-starvation: leaky-bucket that ensures long-tail low-frequency tenants eventually get tokens even under sustained high-priority load.
   - Emergency preemption: for safety-critical enterprise routes (tagged), we preserve immediate preemption rights for a small, auditable set.

Tradeoffs reviewed:
- Complexity vs predictability: soft-share with precedence maximizes utilization but increases complexity for debugging; strict isolation reduces surprises for SREs and customers.
- Observability burden: graceful degradation needs fine-grained telemetry (per-request handoff tags, model-variant health). We must not ship without Console counters and sample traces.
- Downstream UX: customers asked for deterministic behavior when quotas are hit — the team agreed to provide a deterministic degradation ladder per tier in the product docs and expose per-tenant simulation tools in Console.

Decisions (consensus):
- Proceed with Hybrid windows model as the primary architecture for the RFC. Rationale: strikes best balance between utilization and predictable floors for premium tiers.
- Define a three-stage soft-quota handoff: (1) Grace window with handoff header, (2) Automated degradation (batch/quantization/model variant), (3) Throttle with informative error (HTTP 429 + handoff metadata).
- Implement credit buckets with anti-starvation leaky-bucket replenishment. Minimum guaranteed capacity per gold tenant will be defined in billing configuration and enforced at window boundaries.
- Observability must be included in the initial rollout: add per-request handoff tags, per-tenant credit balance gauges, and a Console dashboard (latency, handoff-rate, degraded-request-rate).

Open questions & unresolved items:
- Window sizing: initial suggestion 60s balancing window, but need cluster-level simulation to validate. Action: Evelyn + Marco to run capacity sims (see PLAT-8790).
- How to honor cross-tenant affinity (co-located tenant burst protection) without opening DoS vector. Action: Zach to draft proposal for affinity isolation knobs.
- Billing signals: need clear mapping from degradation steps to billing adjustments (discounts / credits). Action: Priya to sync with Finance and Product.

Action items and owners (short-term):
- Evelyn + Marco: run simulations for 30/60/120s windows and report impact on utilization and gold-tier latency (due 2025-02-20).
- Zach: draft affinity isolation proposal and anti-DoS mitigations (due 2025-02-18).
- Priya: coordinate with Product/Billing for degradation-to-billing mapping; bring back constraints (due 2025-02-19).
- Amina: prototype handoff headers and Console counters in a feature branch; ensure tracing integration for sampled requests (PR to repo by 2025-02-21).

Notes on next steps for the RFC:
- RFC structure: motivation, constraints, policy primitives, state machines for handoff, metrics, rollout plan, migration strategy, safety rollback plan, and testing & simulation results.
- We will target an RFC draft by 2025-02-25. Internal review cycle 1 week, then a design review with SRE and Product.

Meeting artifacts and references:
- Linked tickets and PRs listed above.
- Quick capacity simulation notebook (internal): /shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/sim-notebooks/slo-window-sims.ipynb (note: notebook draft exists in Drive).

Risks called out explicitly:
- Debug surface: adding soft handoffs increases churn in support until Console tooling matures. Mitigation: beta rollout to small set of tenants and clear support playbooks.
- Complexity: hybrid windows introduce timing edge cases during cluster autoscaling. Mitigation: include autoscaler hooks and conservative defaults initially.

Conclusion: team agreed hybrid-window-based SLO tiering with a three-stage soft-quota handoff should become the basis of the RFC. Emphasis on observability and simulation before rollout. Next sync scheduled: Tuesday design-review working session, 2025-02-18 10:00 PT.

Appendix (quick notes):
- Example handoff header: X-Redwood-Handoff: stage=degrade;reason=soft_quota;variant=quantized-v2
- Suggested console panels: per-tenant credit balance, handoff-rate over 1m/5m windows, degradation-latency heatmap by tier.
- Quick glossary: soft-quota = tenant-specific soft limit in tokens/s; grace window = period after soft-quota breach where degraded service is allowed; handoff = transition from normal-serving to degraded serving mode.
